_about: HOME BASE (rule 437(b), rule 347, rule 343; ask lines 356 and 522): YOUR settlement, the one you plant. Read by engine/bohemia_home.js, which the map (slices/BOHEMIA_CITY_WORLD.html __HOME_BASE__) and the town screen read. A modder's file: every word is draft:true (WORDS overwrites), every number is a default HOME BASE set and TUNING owns (rule 38g: no felt number outside the table; this file is the table's row until TUNING folds it in). Realism first: a real settlement lives or dies by WATER, a ROAD, POWER and how near the raiders roam (the coordinator's 11/3 defaults, records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_THE_SETTLEMENT_YOU_PLANT_11_3_26.md).

grade._about: THE SMART SYSTEM (his 'maybe it'll be a smart system'): every block he stands on is graded on four marks, 0 to 3, by how near the nearest block of each kind is (within near[0] blocks a 3, within near[1] a 2, within near[2] a 1, else 0). DANGER reads the other way: 3 is a rival's home or a crew right on top of you. A block is a map cell (om.at), about a quarter mile.

danger._about: the nearest other faction's home base or roaming crew

needs._about: nothing is planted where no water reaches or no road comes in: the people die or nothing trades

grade._first_day_about: never in the first minute (the second votes, 9/23: nothing forced): the PLANT button is offered from the second day of a game

bill._about: YOU RUN IT, SO YOU PAY FOR IT (347(d)): taken at nightfall beside the crew's own bill. keep = the place's own lamp, gate and pump; each person who lives there eats and drinks what a crewman does (per_man_per_night is READ from records/target/bb/nightly_bill.json, never typed here); far water costs more (the vendor's premium, ECONOMY Day 47: water carried in costs a multiple of the pipe).
bill._prize_pays_about: a boss's prize standing at home pays back a day: THE POT's kitchen feeds one, THE TAP's main and THE FILTER's purifier water one (343(b)); counted as batteries off the bill, one each

plan._about: THE PLACE'S OWN GROUND, in house tiles (a combat tile is a house, 9/4), top-down: R a road, L a lot, the front row is the street the map's road comes in on. EVERY LOT FRONTS A ROAD and THE ROADS ARE ONE NETWORK (rule 429(h)); gates/home_base_gate.js fails a lot cut off or a stub split from the rest. Lots open as the place grows: 'open' lots at planting, then 'grow' more each time every open lot has something standing (progress you can see, 347(g)).

prizes._about: A BOSS'S PRIZE STANDS IN YOUR SETTLEMENT (343(b)): read from BohemiaBosses' own state (the verb his kill handed you); the piece is records/target/bb/home_lots.json's, never retyped here

residents._about: THE JOURNEY'S PEOPLE POST UP THERE (347(e)): once a place is planted, a man who leaves the company (let go, or walked when the batteries ran out) goes to live there instead of vanishing, with his face and his name; a spared boss (BOSSES' negotiable ones) and the retinue join the same list when those lanes call add(). Each one eats from the place's bill.

names._about: the place's name until he types his own (draft:true, WORDS); the player does not speak Spanglish, a place's name may

words.plant_sure: Are you sure? This is permanent.

story._about: THE PLACE REMEMBERS (rule 412: 'a lot of your relations and experience with the settlements and your custom settlement will be remembered... they'll tell a story about your granddad'). Every planting, move-in, finished build, prize and name is kept on the place's record; a person who lives there tells it from his own mouth and face (rule 9/20), 'you' in the act it happened, 'your father' one act on, 'your granddad' two on. Words draft:true, WORDS overwrites; the player does not speak Spanglish, the people who live there may.

lines.me_let_go: {Who} let me go on day {day}. I walked here because there was nowhere else.
lines.me_came: I came on day {day}. Somebody said this was a place.
lines.planted: {Who} planted this on day {day}. Everybody said it would never hold.
lines.built: {Who} put up the {what} on day {day}. We still use it.
lines.prize: That {what} came off {name}. {Who} carried it home on day {day}.
lines.named: {Who} named this place {WHAT}. Nobody calls it anything else now.
lines.moved_in: {name} moved in on day {day}. Ask {name} why, not me.
lines.short: Night {day} the batteries ran out. We sat in the dark and nobody left.
lines.given: {WHAT} came to us from {name} on day {day}. It stands out back.

builds._about: WHAT HE BUILDS AT HIS PLACE AND WHY IT MATTERS (rule 343: it changes because of him; rule 441: whole). Every build at his place costs the one battery and the day engine/bohemia_lotbuild.js already charges PLUS the goods below out of the company's supplies (the top bar's own counts, bohemia.supplies.v1), and every morning it stands it puts what it gives into those same supplies, so the top bar moves; a person who lives there works one build each, in lot order, and a worked build gives its 'worked' more. MEASURED FIRST (11/10, the demo): the garden, the tank, the pump and the shed paid one 'resources' a day, a purse currency no screen shows, while their lines said '+1 food/day', '+1 water/day', '+1 tape/day'. Food and water are one count (rule 209). Every number a default HOME BASE set, TUNING's to change; words draft:true.

solar.line: a battery a day off the sun
solar._note: the battery itself is lotbuild's (POWER); a hand on it cleans the panel for one more

stall._note: its clout is lotbuild's; a hand at it trades for food

roof._note: a roof finished brings a family to live there (a resident), who works the next build
